Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

attract verb

draw towards oneself, lure

also draw, lure, entice, attraction, pull in

classical

Cic. Div. 1.86: magnētem lapidem … quī ferrum ad sē adliciat et attrahat (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 2.3.7: successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

alliciō, allicere, allexī, allectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō): with an accusative, often with ad sē · Conjugation on Wiktionary

draw to oneself, attract, lure

Of a magnet drawing iron, and of whatever draws people: money, rewards, kindness, success. Often “entice”, in a bad sense. Frequent in Cicero, never in Terence, Horace or Juvenal (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • attrahō, attrahere, attraxī, attractum — draw towards, drag

    verb, third conjugation, with an accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.86 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 275 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Physical drawing and dragging, of a magnet or of a person brought by force (tribūnōs attrahī ad sē jussit, Liv. 29.9, Lewis & Short); figuratively, drawing someone to a place or a cause.

  • conciliō, conciliāre, conciliāvī, conciliātum — win over, gain (favour, friends)

    verb, first conjugation: the person or thing gained in the accusative, the person won over to in the dative · also used · classical · Liv. 4.48.9: prīmōribus sē patrum concilient (Lewis & Short); Traupman 275 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Attract in the sense of winning goodwill. Its first sense is “bring together, unite” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • magnētem lapidem … quī ferrum ad sē adliciat et attrahat

    the magnet stone, which draws and pulls iron to itselfCic. Div. 1.86 (Lewis & Short)

  • successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

    the success of the wicked lures more people onPhaedr. 2.3.7

  • Cōmis enim et blanda salūtātiō saepe conciliat amīcitiam, inimīcitiam dīluit

    a friendly and pleasant greeting often wins friendship and washes away enmityErasm. Coll., Fōrm., In prīmō congressū, I 3

See also attention.

SourcesLewis & Short: allicio · Lewis & Short: attraho · Lewis & Short: concilio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 275.
